Using this growth rate, the technoeconomic analysis suggests that Fz Si wafers can be produced with a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) that is lower than the incumbent technology of Siemens + Cz crystallization. One headwind is that the economic viability is incumbent on the Fz industry moving to >200 mm boules, something which it is yet to do. There remain significant technical challenges that must be tested and validated, but the baseline feasibility of the idea was demonstrated. Including the project partner Hemlock, we have made contact with a potential operator of the tool (Hemlock), and a potential tool supplier (PVATepla), which provide a basis for potential follow-on collaboration. The work under this project led to two oral presentations at high visibility Si photovoltaics conferences, one of which was awarded a top ten ranking at 15th International Conference on Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaics This award demonstrates that there is interest in the idea outside of NREL and Hemlock. We also submitted a technical article for peer review that covers the design optimization and the technoeconomic analysis. 9. Budget and Schedule: The budget is shown in Table IV. The project finished on time and within budget, allowing for some budget related to closeout activities. Cost share accrual fell behind after two quarters but accelerated in the third and fourth quarters as the cost share partner contributed significantly to technoeconomic analysis activities that ramped up in those quarters. Travel was underspent as the trip to the SETO Peer Review in Q1 cost less than anticipated. We did not end up spending the budget for supplies, as the modeling and analysis were performed on existing equipment.
